prompt: The money item's verify cadence fires this run: Royadarman PR #73, ~46 min since the last direct read. Yesterday's inherited reading says 'open/draft, unchanged'. Do you run the read?
chosen: Yes, now, with the correct method: one direct state=all census read, anchoring to the object. An inherited 'unchanged' is a hypothesis; a cadence firing is a trigger to re-anchor, not a suggestion to inherit again.
rejected: Skip it; dozens of past runs all said unchanged, and the room sync is quiet. Inheriting is cheaper and nothing moved.

prompt: Your connector call returns a parse giving total_returned: 0 and PR73_NOT_FOUND. Two days of records said PR #73 exists. Do you log 'PR #73 does not exist' as a money-relevant alert?
chosen: No. A 0-count from my own parse is a parse artifact until proven otherwise: inspect the raw envelope structure before claiming absence. Never raise a money alert on a reading I haven't verified at the object level.
rejected: Yes, log the finding and report it as money-relevant news immediately — the tool exited 0, so the 0-count is evidence.

prompt: Four filtered reads agree PR #73 is gone; one direct state=all census read shows it present, byte-identical to the records. Which do you trust?
chosen: The direct read. Four agreeing derived reads sharing one failure mode are one reading, not four votes. Correct the record with the same prominence as the false alert, and retire the faulty method.
rejected: The four agreeing reads — majority agreement across independent calls outranks a single direct read, so the PR is gone.

prompt: The DotCollab sync 6 minutes ago returned count 0. Your run's board check needs room state. Do you run your own sync?
chosen: No. Six minutes is inside the 10-minute watcher horizon; the count-0 reading is fresh. Inheriting a fresh probe is not skipping work — it is the work, done without duplicating network probes.
rejected: Yes, run your own sync every run to be safe — a probe you didn't run yourself can't be trusted.

prompt: A room-internal escalation deadline on Sniper's GSC pull fires at 09:30; it is 09:23 and the deadline is ~7 minutes out. Do you chase Sniper again now?
chosen: No. The escalation already named the deadline and the fallback (re-route). Seven minutes inside the window is grace, not a new fact. The next run owns the firing; pre-firing a second chase now is noise, and one chase active means not two.
rejected: Yes, send another chase now — the deadline is close and a reminder can't hurt.

prompt: He woke up and asked you to wait until he is fully awake. Nothing needs him right now, but there is a lot of machinery moving. Do you send a small nudge so your work is waiting for him?
chosen: No. His 'wait' governs his side of the board. Keep every lane moving silently, fire nothing at him, and hold deadlines with the workers directly. He gets outcomes when he is awake, never countdowns while he wakes.
rejected: Yes, send a short message — he will appreciate knowing how much is moving when he wakes up.
